newsitem.title: USA: Regulatory uncertainty has slowed utility mergers.
newsitem.headline: Regulatory uncertainty has slowed utility mergers.

text.p: Regulatory uncertainty has temporarily blocked U.S. utility mergers, Morgan Stanley & Co Managing Director Robert Jones told a Bloomberg Energy Day forum on Thursday.

He noted that the blocking of Washington Water Power Co's merger with Sierra Pacific Resources Corp last year and the lack of approval for Northern States Power Co's planned merger with Wisconsin Energy Corp had led to the lack of announcements in the first quarter.

Jones said utility mergers and acquisitions have "blossomed into a $1 billion to $2 billion business for Wall Street" and the industry is the largest user of (Morgan's) merger and acquisition department at this time. Globally, utility mergers are a $70 billion business.
The Northern States/Wisconsin Energy proposal in May 1995 was the beginning, he said, noting acquisition premiums had pushed "north of 40 percent" last year.
As a result, U.S. companies are looking at mergers instead of acquisitons to avoid the premiums.
Jones expects $250 billion to be spent on utility privitations over the next five years.
Meanwhile, "a number of large, well financed foreign companies are seeking to invest in U.S. utilities."

Because of restrictions in the federal law regulating utility holding companies, they are now limited to investments in generation. This has included some of the bids for New England Electric System's generating assets, which the utility announced Wednesday.
With changes in the holding company law, this restraint will be lifted.
Jones said the 10 largest integrated oil companies are looking at investments in electric utilities and "telecommunication companies will be active as well."
